html:
An alliance of indigenous villages on the plains of west central Taiwan, around modern Taichung, shown on the map in 1700. It is known mostly from Dutch records of the 17th century, which call its ruler the Lord of Middag.

The alliance joined villages of several Austronesian peoples, among them the Papora, Babuza and Pazeh, under a hereditary chief. It resisted Dutch Formosa for years before making terms, and was later attacked by the Kingdom of Tungning, in 1670. Under Qing rule Chinese settlers took more and more of its land, and after a failed revolt in 1731 and 1732 the alliance broke up. Its peoples were part of Taiwan's indigenous peoples.
